title: SmartShelf product catalogue
description: public/data/catalogue.json — the resolved product population the artefact's capabilities were computed over. Published beside dashboard.json by the same run, never inside it: it carries no computed figure, and the daily surface needs none of it. ADR-024. Every price here is THE STORE'S OWN; this file contains no competitor price and no figure derived from one.

generated_at.description: The run that produced this file. Must equal dashboard.json's for the same run.

inputs_digest.description: The artefact's own inputs_digest, carried so a reader can PROVE the two files came from one run rather than assume it. The pages fetch them separately and a failed catalogue write leaves a stale file beside a fresh artefact; comparing the digests is how that is detected rather than believed.

population.description: ADR-020. Which catalogue the run counted over, identical to the artefact's.

pos.description: vintages.pos as the artefact publishes it — file, as_of and as_of_source. A product list with no export date behind it is not evidence of anything.

count.description: Null when products is null. 0 is a legitimate count here, unlike elsewhere: an empty LIST is a claim the engine only makes when it loaded the products and there were none. Not knowing is expressed by null on both fields together.

products.description: Null when the engine could not load the population — never [] for that case, which would read as 'the store has no products'. Sorted by barcode then product_name so the bytes repeat night to night and git stores the file once.

barcode.description: Null for a barcode-less row, which ADR-022 identifies by name instead.

shelf_price.description: THE STORE'S OWN price on the shelf. Null where the export carries none. D-3: a product with no shelf price has no shelf price, and 0 would read as free.

delivery_price.description: THE STORE'S OWN price on Wolt — `wolt_price` from its POS export, not a rival's. Both prices in this file belong to YomYom, and F1 exists because the two disagree. Mapping this to a competitor field would tell the owner a rival is undercutting him with his own price: a two-character change that lights a page instantly and lies. Competitor prices are not in this file at all — they reach the surface through the `competitor_position` capability, computed from scraped observations, a different input entirely.

cost_source.description: How the cost was arrived at, so a reader can tell a declared cost from a derived one.

recorded_stock.description: Raw, negative values included — F2's whole subject. Carries no money: D-1 forbids a shekel figure on a stock quantity.
